name: Leviathan Bluff
geological_features: Atmospheric cliff formations where cloud layers terminate abruptly
A ring system of extraordinary width composed of captured moon fragments
Permanent aurora displays at both poles
Core-generated electromagnetic pulses at irregular intervals
specific_features: Electromagnetic pulses that disrupt systems across the entire planetary system
description: Leviathan Bluff is a near-superjovian gas giant whose sheer mass dominates its entire planetary system. Its atmosphere displays a unique phenomenon: cloud layers that terminate abruptly at certain altitudes, creating the appearance of vast atmospheric cliffs or bluffs where one color band ends and another begins with no gradual transition. The effect is as if the atmosphere were layered in discrete, stacked plates.

The planet's ring system is spectacular, composed of the fragmented remains of moons that strayed within the Roche limit. Aurora displays at both poles are permanent and intense, visible across the system as twin beacons of green and violet. The overall impression is of a world too large and too powerful to be safely approached.

At irregular intervals, Leviathan Bluff's core generates electromagnetic pulses of sufficient power to disrupt unshielded electronics across the entire planetary system. The pulses have no predictable pattern and have caused significant damage to orbital infrastructure. The mechanism is believed to involve phase transitions in the metallic hydrogen core, but the irregularity defies modeling.

Despite its hazards, Leviathan Bluff's antimatter traces make it a target of enormous strategic interest. The electromagnetic pulses, however, make sustained operations nearly impossible with current shielding technology. Several attempts to establish permanent harvesting infrastructure have been abandoned after pulse events destroyed the investments. The planet remains a prize that no one has yet been able to claim.
